name: Bun nuoc leo
summary: Bún nước lèo is served in Can Tho and is not a Can Tho invention on these accounts. Vietnam Tourism’s dining page says the noodle hails from Soc Trang, 60 km southeast, with a fish-stock broth, and that a Vietnamese version uses pickled river fish, shrimp, roasted pork, crackling, fish balls, herbs, soy beans, and banana blossom. The four-day piece eats the bowl in Tra Vinh before the transfer. The Mỹ Khánh article also names it.
origin: Soc Trang on the dining page. Served on Đề Thám in Can Tho and at Mỹ Khánh. Also eaten in Tra Vinh on the four-day piece.
howToEat: A noodle bowl. A clock for the Can Tho bowl was not printed. Check on arrival.
where: Đề Thám, the street the dining page names in Can Tho.
Mỹ Khánh, on the department article.
Tra Vinh, on the four-day piece, before Can Tho.
seoTitle: Bun nuoc leo served in Can Tho
seoDescription: A Soc Trang noodle, 60 km southeast, served on Đề Thám and at Mỹ Khánh, and eaten in Tra Vinh on Vietnam Tourism’s four-day piece.
